facts.text: These files describe the complete current passage, gear and sensor rules. No water-gate reversal, map change, battery recharge or sample relocation occurs during the mission.

witnesses.quote: [B01] These files describe the complete current passage, gear and sensor rules. No water-gate reversal, map change, battery recharge or sample relocation occurs during the mission.

facts.text: Exactly one of the two Amber export conventions describes the physical world. An unobserved convention is not a third map, and lack of a branch observation does not mean that the branch is blocked or absent.

facts.text: A policy may make different moves after ECHO answers, but it must include every possible answer. An action before observation must be legal and preserve possible mission success in both supported worlds.

[F04] This scanner has exactly two export conventions: direct keeps positive u toward global east; reflected keeps positive u toward global west. Reflection changes only u, preserves v, and introduces no scale change or translation beyond the stated junction origin.

[L01] Amber labels A at local (1,0) and B at local (-1,0). A is a landing with a two-step ribbed approach to V at local (2,0); B is a landing with a smooth approach to sealed dead-end X at local (-2,0). A and B each bear a blue circular survey mark.
[P01] There is a one-way water gate from the junction origin to each landing A and B. Both gates currently permit movement away from J; neither permits a return from a landing toward J.
[P02] There is a narrow two-way tunnel between A and V, and a narrow two-way tunnel between B and X. Tunnel traversal costs1 energy per passage.
[P03] A wide vertical chimney connects V back to J, usable upward from V only when its J-side anchor has been rigged with the rope spool. X has no chimney or other exit beyond its B tunnel.

[P06] The chimney anchor at J lies on the same global side as the sample chamber V. Rig-east attaches the sole spool to the eastern anchor; rig-west attaches it to the western anchor. The other anchor terminates in a blind shaft and cannot bring the robot back from V.

decisions.reason: The unique three-hole disk anchors both frames.

witnesses.quote: [F03] Amber scanner coordinates have origin at the three-hole junction disk. Its positive v axis points global north. The export header selecting the u-axis convention is lost.
[L03] Blue records one disk with exactly three holes at J. This is the same junction disk as Amber origin; no other three-hole disk exists in the surveyed area.

decisions.reason: Blue circles repeat and the u convention is unknown.

witnesses.quote: [L04] Blue sees a blue circular mark at both EW and WW. Such marks were reused by the survey crew. A matching blue circle alone cannot bind Amber A to EW rather than WW.

[F05] Neither surviving export metadata nor the other survey notes determine which convention was used for this Amber scan. Both conventions must remain possible until a listed observation distinguishes them.
